breaks.Break_Summary: The required end-to-end production chain needs a higher or more uniform availability/SLA boundary than the exact proposed NiCE module mix provides.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Exact product/SKU dependency map, failover path and fallback process must be designed and tested.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show the exact contracted SLA, dependencies, regional architecture and degraded-mode behavior for every component in our critical customer path.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Future product changes require regression/failover testing across the dependency chain.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential additional licensing, redundancy, carrier, integration and testing cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: More modules and fallback paths increase incident and support coordination.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate the proposed architecture if a critical required component cannot meet the buyer's minimum availability/recovery requirement and no economically rational mitigation exists.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Redesign the critical path; select higher-SLA product family; add fallback/redundancy; or contract compensating architecture and service commitments.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: SLA table, product-family, acquisition integration, or regional architecture change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: A buyer requires a non-negotiable availability target across routing plus one or more AI/WFM/analytics/legacy extension modules whose contracted SLA or dependency behavior is below that target.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Large enterprise, BPO or regulated transformation
breaks.Break_Summary: The platform remains capable, but bespoke routing, legacy integration, data migration, WFM/QM and AI scope can push delivery into high or transformational Implementation Gravity.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Discovery, architecture, code/configuration, migration, integration, test automation, UAT, training and governance work expand materially.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Separate native configuration, low-code, custom Snippet code, partner-built integration and vendor PS for every workflow in our design.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Later changes can require developer/partner effort and paid PS for customer-specific configuration.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Higher transformation services and internal program cost; potential change orders.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Custom assets require ongoing ownership and regression testing.
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose another architecture if the required customization/services dependency exceeds the buyer's implementation tolerance or cannot fit the required timeline without unacceptable risk.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Standardize processes, phase the program, use packaged connectors/migration accelerators, reduce custom Studio code and assign a named delivery/Day-2 operating model.
breaks.Ownership_During_Implementation: Customer + Certified Implementation Partner/SI + NiCE PS as scoped
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Studio/low-code architecture, implementation tooling, services terms or migration accelerators materially change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer combines complex custom routing, multiple systems of record, migration from heavily customized legacy platforms, AI/knowledge/action workflows and WFM/QM transformation under an aggressive timeline.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Seasonal operations, BPOs, fast-changing transformation programs and cost-sensitive buyers
breaks.Break_Summary: The solution is technically viable, but multi-component licensing, commitments, peak concurrency, AI consumption, telephony and services can become economically irrational for a volatile or under-utilized operating model.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Commercial modeling, usage telemetry, contract protections and governance are required.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Model our actual demand distribution against named/concurrent users, minimum commitments, AI conversations, telephony, add-ons, storage/media and PS; show downside and upside cases.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Expansion, seasonality and AI adoption can change the cost curve nonlinearly.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential overcommit, burst, AI-consumption, telephony, add-on and services costs.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Requires ongoing usage and invoice governance.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate or redesign if risk-adjusted three-year TCO exceeds the buyer's approved threshold after realistic transformation and run-state costs.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Model 36-month platform/transformation/run-state TCO, negotiate ramps/true-down/caps/reallocation, phase AI, and instrument actual usage before expansion.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Pricing, packaging, AI metering, commitment or services terms change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer has seasonal/volatile concurrency, uncertain AI volumes, long AI interactions, high test traffic, heavy add-on use or limited ability to negotiate ramp/true-down protections.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Lean IT/contact-center teams or organizations unwilling to fund platform ownership
breaks.Break_Summary: CXone can become a poor operating fit when the buyer lacks the technical/admin ownership needed for support, complex routing, integrations, AI and ongoing optimization.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Operating model, escalation process, change ownership and governance must be designed, not assumed.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show who realistically owns first-tier support, routing changes, custom Studio, integrations, AI changes, release testing and incident diagnosis after go-live.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Future changes remain slower/costlier if internal ownership does not mature.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Additional admin, managed-services, developer and governance labor.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Day-2 burden persists and can create vendor/partner dependency.
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose another platform or a managed operating model if the buyer will not staff the required ownership and the external operating model is not economically acceptable.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Simplify scope, use managed services/partner operations, train named platform owners, or reduce custom code and integration depth.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Admin tooling, support duties, managed-service model or low-code capability changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer expects a mostly vendor-operated platform, has minimal technical administration/developer capacity, and still requires bespoke routing/integration/AI complexity.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Enterprise platform-consolidation and strategic standardization programs
breaks.Break_Summary: A broad 'one platform' consolidation thesis can break when acquired, legacy and current product families retain distinct architecture, SLA, metering, support or migration boundaries.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Architecture, commercial and migration decisions must be made by exact product family, not brand.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Map every proposed module to supplier/product family, architecture, SLA, data plane, admin plane, pricing unit, support owner and migration roadmap.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Future consolidation/retirement can force migration and regression work.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential duplicate licensing, migration, integration, support and exit cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Multiple product families can preserve parallel admin/support boundaries.
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose a different architecture if the buyer's required simplification, portability or single-control-plane objective cannot be met by the exact proposed product mix.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Create a product-lineage and dependency contract; choose current target families; define migration state; require data/config portability and support/SLA ownership per component.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Acquisition integration, product consolidation, SKU retirement or migration-roadmap change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer's business case assumes that CXone, Cognigy, IEX, LiveVox or legacy analytics/QM components behave as one uniform control, support and commercial plane.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Disable or degrade one critical dependency/module at a time during a buyer-scripted interaction flow.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Timestamped logs, support events, routing outcomes, recovery evidence and contract SLA mapping.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Unrecoverable customer-path failure, loss of required state/recording/routing, or recovery beyond threshold.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: Ask a comparable customer which module or dependency caused the most consequential production outage and how recovery actually worked.
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Final SKU/dependency map, target RTO/RPO/availability, carrier/integration dependencies.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Critical-path availability and degraded-mode behavior differ by exact module/dependency chain.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Required interactions continue in the agreed degraded mode and recover within buyer thresholds.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Buyer supplies three routing changes: routine queue, moderately complex policy change, bespoke exception flow. Vendor must implement live and classify ownership.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Screen capture, code/config artifacts, time-to-change, owner and testing steps.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Vendor cannot reproduce the workflow without undisclosed code/services or buyer autonomy is materially lower than represented.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: What routing/workflow change still requires developers or professional services six months after go-live?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Buyer routing scenarios and admin personas.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Demo may hide which routing/workflow changes require custom code or PS.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Vendor completes routine changes at the claimed admin level and transparently identifies code/PS-dependent steps.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Price buyer-provided low/base/high 36-month workload scenarios with all mandatory modules, telephony, AI, support and implementation assumptions.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Workbook, quote/order form, unit definitions, caps, ramps, true-down/reallocation terms.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Material cost categories are excluded, undefined, or cannot be reconciled to contract terms.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: How did actual year-two invoice compare with the procurement model, and which line items expanded unexpectedly?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Monthly agents/concurrency, contacts, minutes, digital messages, AI conversations, testing, storage, geographies.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Commercial model may become unpredictable under concurrency, usage and AI variability.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: All three scenarios reconcile to contract units and expose downside protections/caps/ramp assumptions.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Reference must match buyer scale, integrations and module mix; quantify internal roles and external dependencies.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Role counts, change examples, support escalation and service usage.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Reference cannot quantify ownership or materially contradicts proposed operating model.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: How many internal people administer the platform, what requires developers/partners, and what do you wish you had staffed earlier?
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Buyer may underestimate Day-2 staffing and support ownership.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Reference can name actual FTE/roles, support escalation process, changes self-managed and changes requiring partner/vendor.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Vendor provides an architecture/product-lineage schedule for every proposed SKU.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Any material module remains ambiguous or 'platform-level' without exact contractual mapping.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: Which products in your current NiCE estate still behave like separate product families operationally or contractually?
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Suite branding can obscure product lineage and operating boundaries.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Every SKU maps to product family, architecture, data plane, admin plane, SLA, support owner, pricing unit and migration state.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Run a buyer-scale export of interaction metadata, historical reporting data and recording media while normal operations continue.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: API logs, timestamps, record counts, media checksums and estimated full-volume duration/cost.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Throttling, licensing or latency prevents required operational/exit objective.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: How long did your largest historical media/data export take and what rate limits or extra SKUs surprised you?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Representative record/media volume and target export window.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Data/media portability may not meet buyer freshness or exit-volume requirements.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Completes within buyer latency/throughput threshold with documented reconciliation and known cost.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Load buyer historical voice + asynchronous/digital work, forecast, schedule, intraday-adjust and compare against buyer baseline.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Forecast outputs, error distributions, schedules, admin changes and exception handling.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Model cannot represent workload physics, or required changes depend on unacceptable external services.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: What workload types were hardest to forecast after deployment and how much planner effort is still required?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: 12+ months demand, backlog, service goals, staffing constraints and exception history.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: WFM depth must match buyer workload physics, not algorithm count.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Forecast/schedule performs within buyer-set error/service thresholds and admins can explain/adjust drivers.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Buyer creates a blind gold set, validates human rubric/ground truth, then compares AI scoring across normal/edge cases and demographic/linguistic slices where lawful.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Per-item scores, evidence/justification, confusion/error distribution, overrides and drift plan.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Fails accuracy/calibration threshold or cannot support appropriate human review/override.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: Where did Auto Score disagree most with calibrated human QA and what did you change?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Representative interactions, validated rubric and adjudicated human truth set.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Auto Score feature existence does not prove measurement validity.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Meets buyer-defined error/calibration thresholds; disagreements are explainable and reviewable; downstream use is governed.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Use buyer knowledge containing current, stale and conflicting sources; run live representative contacts and measure timing, grounding, usefulness and agent reliance.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Assist timing, source citations, accept/reject behavior, errors and outcome measures.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Late/ungrounded/confidently wrong assist exceeds buyer threshold or agent cannot meaningfully challenge it.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: Which assist types do agents ignore or mistrust most, and how do you measure appropriate reliance rather than adoption?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Governed knowledge corpus, edge cases, novice/experienced agent cohorts.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Copilot may be correct but late, distracting, poorly grounded or over-trusted.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Buyer-set accuracy/timing/grounding thresholds met; agents can inspect/reject; incorrect assists do not drive unsafe action.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Run authenticated action scenarios with duplicate request, timeout, partial backend success, stale state, revoked permission and human-approval cases.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Action log, identity/permission trace, transaction state, rollback/compensation and incident record.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Silent partial success, duplicate action, unauthorized action, missing audit, or no safe recovery.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: Which production agentic failure created the most repair work, and how was it detected and contained?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Sandbox systems/tools with reversible transactions and audit access.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Agentic/workflow action claims require transaction and failure integrity.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Correct permissioning, no duplicate harmful action, transaction completion verified, failures detected, compensation/rollback and human escalation work.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Create two isolated client programs sharing a subset of agents; use different routing, recording/retention, integrations, QA/WFM policies and reporting; spike/fail one client's dependency.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Tenant/config maps, user/agent behavior, usage/billing output, failure telemetry and client reporting.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Isolation leak, duplicate licensing destroys model, usage cannot be allocated, or incident blast radius crosses client boundary.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: How do you prevent one client's config/integration incident or traffic spike from affecting another client, and how do you prove that isolation?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Two synthetic clients, shared-agent pool, distinct policies and cost centers.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Detailed BPO multi-client operating mechanics are unverified.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: No cross-client data/config leakage; shared-agent experience works; usage is attributable; one client failure does not materially affect the other beyond agreed boundary.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Run buyer-critical CRM/Epic workflows including authentication expiration, field mismatch, dependency outage and vendor release version change.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Transaction traces, logs, support RACI and recovery time.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Critical workflow unavailable or failure becomes an unsupported vendor-boundary dispute.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: When a critical CRM/EHR connector fails, who owns diagnosis first and what does your support contract actually cover?
proof_requirements.Required_Test_Data_or_Preconditions: Target systems, representative permissions, sandbox data.
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Prebuilt system-of-record integration may not equal required workflow depth/supportability.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: All required read/write/actions work; failures are visible; support owner is unambiguous; recovery meets threshold.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Provision representative inbound/outbound numbers/call paths in required countries, test BYOC and carrier failover.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Call records, MOS/quality, failover trace, carrier path and porting plan.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: A required country/use case depends on unsupported/uneconomic workaround.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: Which country or number type required the most nonstandard carrier work in your deployment?
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Global voice claim must map to the buyer's actual countries and carriers.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Required countries, number types, CLI/emergency/regulatory needs and failover pass.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Load buyer-like CRM context, multiple digital sessions, AI assist, supervisor monitoring and escalation; require novice agents/supervisors to execute tasks.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Task time, clicks/context switches, errors, supervisor intervention and user feedback.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Critical context/action unavailable, high latency, or excessive workflow fragmentation.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: What parts of the desktop did you have to simplify or customize after agents used it at scale?
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Unified agent/supervisor workspace must remain usable under real buyer complexity.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Users complete tasks within buyer thresholds without losing context; supervisor controls work without excessive surface switching.

proof_requirements.Buyer_Controlled_Scenario: Use a comparable customer reference focused on discovery, migration, integrations, testing, PS and change orders.
proof_requirements.Evidence_to_Capture: Planned vs actual timeline, PS, internal FTE, change-order categories and hypercare duration.
proof_requirements.Failure_Criterion: Reference unavailable or material variances cannot be explained relative to proposed SOW.
proof_requirements.Reference_Call_Question: What did the original SOW underestimate, what caused the largest change order, and which implementation work persisted into Day 2?
proof_requirements.Risk_or_Hypothesis: Planned implementation burden may diverge from actual SOW/change-order reality.
proof_requirements.Success_Criterion: Reference provides planned vs actual timeline/services/internal labor and identifies major variances.
